headline: Pacific Bluefin Tuna Gets New Protection as Nations Agree on Harvest Strategy
meta_description: After a decade of recovery, Pacific bluefin tuna now has science-based long-term protection, with automatic safeguards if populations decline.
summary_short: Countries managing Pacific fisheries approved a landmark harvest strategy for bluefin tuna, allowing sustainable catches while protecting against future decline.
body:
At its annual meeting in Lisbon from August 31 to September 4, the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission (IATTC) approved a long-term harvest strategy for Pacific bluefin tuna—a species that had collapsed to just 2.6% of its historic population a decade ago but has since made a remarkable recovery. The new strategy, adopted after 10 years of research, allows for modest increases in catches while automatically triggering fishing reductions should the population decline. The agreement represents a critical safeguard for a species managed jointly with another Pacific fisheries body, the WCPFC, since bluefin tuna form a single population spanning the entire Pacific Ocean.

The timing of this protective measure is deliberate. Dave Gershman, a senior officer at The Pew Charitable Trusts who observed the negotiations, explained the logic: "You want to have these things in place when times are good so it's there when you need it." The plan was proposed by Japan, the United States, and Mexico after intensive collaboration between both regional management organizations. For the strategy to work fully, the WCPFC will need to adopt complementary rules at its own meeting scheduled for November 30 to December 4 in Vanuatu.

However, the commission fell short in another area. Members failed to reach consensus on a proposed multispecies harvest strategy for bigeye, yellowfin, and skipjack tuna—species that are often caught together. This framework would have been the world's first to trigger fishing restrictions across multiple species if any one population declined. While industry groups and sustainability advocates pushed for adoption, opposition from countries seeking greater fishing capacity blocked the measure, which requires unanimous agreement under IATTC rules.
quick_facts: Pacific bluefin tuna recovered from 2.6% of historic population to healthy levels
Strategy allows catch increases with automatic reductions if decline occurs
Managed jointly by IATTC and WCPFC across entire Pacific Ocean
Proposal led by Japan, U.S., and Mexico after 10 years of research
